meta.title: Operation of Mechanical Shaker in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide continuous controlled mechanical agitation for maceration extraction, percolation, and solubility testing of crude drugs and plant extracts in the Pharmacognosy laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for cold maceration extraction, dissolution testing, and preparation of filtered herbal solutions where extended mechanical agitation improves yield.
procedure: Inspect the mechanical shaker platform, clamps, and spring holders for wear and cleanliness before use.
Select appropriate flasks or bottles for the extraction — ensure they fit securely in the available clamps.
Prepare the plant material + solvent mixture in the flasks: add the weighed powdered drug, then add the specified volume of extraction solvent.
Cap the flasks tightly with PTFE-lined caps or parafilm-wrapped stoppers to prevent evaporation.
Place flasks symmetrically on the shaker platform to distribute the load evenly.
Secure each flask with the spring clips or holddown brackets — test by gently pushing each flask to confirm it is locked.
Set the speed using the RPM control knob: 100–150 RPM for maceration extraction; 200–250 RPM for vigorous mixing.
Set the timer for the required extraction duration: typically 24–72 hours for maceration extraction; 1–4 hours for dissolution/solubility tests.
Switch on the shaker and confirm it operates smoothly without excessive vibration or erratic movement.
Periodically check that all flasks remain secured during extended runs — check every few hours for long extractions.
At the end of the extraction, switch off and wait for the platform to stop completely.
Remove flasks carefully — contents may be under slight pressure; loosen caps slowly.
Filter the extract immediately through Whatman No. 1 or No. 41 filter paper in a Buchner funnel.
Measure and record the filtrate volume and note the yield.
Clean the platform with a damp cloth; use 70% ethanol for solvent residues.
precautions: Load the shaker platform symmetrically — asymmetric loads cause dangerous vibration and motor strain.
Do not exceed the rated weight capacity of the platform.
Ensure all flasks are tightly stoppered before shaking — solvent leaks create hazardous wet patches on the platform and floor.
For flammable organic solvents, use the shaker inside a fume hood or ensure the lab is well ventilated.
Do not operate at maximum speed for extended periods continuously — allow cooling breaks.
Always wait for the platform to stop before removing flasks.
Do not use cracked flasks — mechanical agitation exacerbates existing cracks leading to failure during shaking.
